01:4ACC.note: Four little-endian RGB555 colours, $5E4D, $7FFF, $66F2 and $0000: one CGB palette of four colours. LoadPalette0FromData copies it to wBGPaletteBuffer, sets wBGPaletteUploadRequest to $7F, copies it to wBGPaletteBuffer a second time and sets wOBJPaletteUploadRequest to $7F, all only when wIsCGB is non-zero. The bank $02 copy of the routine (LoadPalette0FromData_Bank02) sends its second copy to wOBJPaletteBuffer instead. (C1, E-0381)

01:5364.name: DebugSkillViewer_Update_DrawFlagBits_Data
01:5364.note: Eight single-bit masks $80, $40, $20, $10, $08, $04, $02, $01, indexed by the tile number 0-7 counted from the left. DebugSkillViewer_Update_DrawFlagBits tests the flag byte in D against each mask, most significant bit first, and writes tile C + 1 for a set bit and tile C for a clear bit to B consecutive VRAM cells starting at HL. (C1, E-0381)

01:555C.name: DebugResultsDisplay_ResistanceAddress_Data1
01:555C.note: Two BG map addresses, $9986 and $99A6 (vBGMap0 row 12, column 6 and row 13, column 6). DebugResultsDisplay_ResistanceAddress uses this pair when wDebugCursor is 4 (the first parent): the first word for a resistance number wSharedMenuWork below 14, the second word for 14 and above (number minus 14), and it adds the remaining number to the address as a column offset. The 27 resistance digits are therefore a row of 14 and a row of 13. (C1, E-0381)

01:5560.name: DebugResultsDisplay_ResistanceAddress_Data2
01:5560.note: Two BG map addresses, $99E6 and $9A06 (vBGMap0 row 15, column 6 and row 16, column 6): the same two-row layout of the 27 resistance digits for the other parent, used by DebugResultsDisplay_ResistanceAddress when wDebugCursor is not 4. The index is wSharedMenuWork as for DebugResultsDisplay_ResistanceAddress_Data1. (C1, E-0381)

01:5B70.name: DebugResultsDisplay_DrawSelectedField_Data1
01:5B70.note: Ten words, indexed by the field number wDebugCursor (0-9): each is the address of the RAM value that field shows. They are wDebugValue0, wDebugValue2, wDebugValue3, wDebugSubState, wScreenStep, wScreenCounter, wGlyphListStart, wScreenSubStep, wGlyphListPos and wGridCursorX. DebugResultsDisplay_DrawSelectedField loads the word stored there into BC and draws it as hex digits, a one-tile value or two decimal digits depending on the field. (C1, E-0381)

01:5B84.name: DebugResultsDisplay_DrawSelectedField_Data2
01:5B84.note: Ten BG map addresses, indexed by the field number wDebugCursor (0-9), where the breeding debug screen draws that field: fields 0-3 at vBGMap0 rows 7-10, column 6 ($98E6, $9906, $9926, $9946) and fields 4-9 at rows 12-17, column 2 ($9982, $99A2, ... $9A22). DebugResultsDisplay_DrawSelectedField draws the value there and StepDebugCursorDebugCounter_BlankField blanks three cells from it during the blink. (C1, E-0381)

01:5DAD.name: DebugAutomap_Update_Data
01:5DAD.note: Thirteen map ids: $00, $05, $20, $30, $48, $70, $A0, $A8, $B0, $B8, $C8, $D1, $DA. When bit 7 of wDebugSubState is set, DebugAutomap_Update (B pressed) stores the entry at index wDebugState & $1F into hMapId and enters the field (game mode 1, wMapType 0). wDebugState is byte 0 of the chosen wKeyList entry, and the index is masked to 0-31, so the reader does not stop at the thirteenth entry. (C1, E-0381)

01:68D3.name: DebugBattleSetup_Update_HandleInput_Data
01:68D3.note: Twelve BG map addresses, $9887, $98A7, ... $99E7 (vBGMap0 rows 4 to 15, column 7, one per row), indexed by the field number wMenuState (0-11) of the debug battle set-up screen. DebugBattleSetup_Update_HandleInput blinks the selected value there and DrawDebugValueHexForMenuState redraws the field value (the word of wWorkBuf + 2 * wMenuState) there as three hex digits. (C1, E-0381)

01:68EB.name: DebugBattleSetup_WrapValueAfterStep_Data
01:68EB.note: Twelve little-endian words, indexed by the field number wMenuState (0-11): the largest value each battle set-up field may take, $0002, $02AB, $02AB, $02AB, $0001, $0000, $0140, $0063, $0140, $0063, $0140, $0063. DebugBattleSetup_WrapValueAfterStep and DebugBattleSetup_WrapValueAfterBigStep wrap a value stepped below 0 to this limit and a value above the limit to 0. (C1, E-0381)

01:6A6C.name: DebugBattleSetupShowFieldString_Data1
01:6A6C.note: Three VRAM glyph-tile addresses, vTiles2 + $200, + $2A0 and + $330 ($9200, $92A0, $9330), indexed by wMenuState - 1 for fields 1-3 (the three monsters). DebugBattleSetupShowFieldString puts one in wTextWindowTileLo/Hi with a window of 9 tiles by 1 row ($0901) before ShowString_Bank88 draws the name of the monster there. (C1, E-0381)

01:6A72.name: DebugBattleSetupShowFieldString_Data2
01:6A72.note: Three VRAM glyph-tile addresses, vTiles2 + $4E0, + $570 and + $600 ($94E0, $9570, $9600), indexed by (wMenuState - 6) / 2 for fields 6, 8 and 10. DebugBattleSetupShowFieldString uses each as the 9 by 1 text window where ShowString_Bank08 draws the string whose index is the low byte of that field and whose category is the high byte + 2. (C1, E-0381)

01:6A78.name: DebugBattleSetupShowFieldString_Data3
01:6A78.note: Three BG map addresses, $996B, $99AB and $99EB (vBGMap0 rows 11, 13 and 15, column 11), indexed by (wMenuState - 7) / 2 for fields 7, 9 and 11. DebugBattleSetupShowFieldString writes the low byte of that field there as two decimal digit tiles ($10 + tens digit, $10 + ones digit). (C1, E-0381)

01:6EB0.name: DebugBattleSetup_ClearKeyList_Data
01:6EB0.note: A block of $80 bytes all $FF: 32 four-byte wKeyList entries filled with the end marker $FF. DebugBattleSetup_ClearKeyList copies all of it over wKeyList (32 times 4 bytes) to empty the key list. (C1, E-0381)

02:4322.name: LoadPalette0FromData_Bank02_Data
02:4322.note: Four little-endian RGB555 colours, $7C00 (pure blue), $7FFF (white), $01E0 (a mid green) and $0000 (black): one CGB palette. LoadPalette0FromData_Bank02 copies it to wBGPaletteBuffer and to wOBJPaletteBuffer and sets wBGPaletteUploadRequest and wOBJPaletteUploadRequest to $7F, only when wIsCGB is non-zero. (C1, E-0381)

02:4510.name: BrightenFieldMenuColors_Data
02:4510.note: Nine amounts, $04, $08, ... $24 in steps of 4, indexed by the frame number wScreenCounter. BrightenFieldMenuColors adds the amount to each 5-bit blue, green and red part of the colours of the warp effect palette and caps each part at 31. wScreenCounter wraps to 0 after 7 in the caller, so this reader uses only $04-$20 and never reaches the last byte $24. (C1, E-0381)

02:45C2.name: WriteCGBObjPaletteFromDMGShadesDMGPaletteOBP0_Data
02:45C2.note: Four byte offsets, $02, $04, $00, $06, indexed by a 2-bit DMG shade (0-3): the byte offset of the colour in the four-colour source palette at HL that stands for that shade (shade 0 takes colour 1, shade 1 colour 2, shade 2 colour 0, shade 3 colour 3). WriteCGBObjPaletteFromDMGShadesDMGPaletteOBP0 takes each of the four 2-bit fields of wDMGPaletteOBP0 in turn, adds the offset to HL and writes that colour word to rOBPD. (C1, E-0381)

02:4AD6.name: GameMode1_Init_Data1
02:4AD6.note: One byte, $00: the Super Game Boy palette set number. GameMode1_Init copies it to wSGBPaletteSet before it calls SendSGBPaletteSetPacket. (C1, E-0381)

02:4AD7.name: GameMode1_Init_Data2
02:4AD7.note: One byte, $00: the Super Game Boy attribute file number. GameMode1_Init copies it to wSGBAttrFile before it calls SendSGBPaletteSetPacket. (C1, E-0381)

02:5205.name: RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_SwapTilePairs_Data
02:5205.note: Twelve four-byte entries, each two little-endian VRAM tile addresses (vTiles2 + 16 * tile number): tiles $1C/$1E, $1D/$1F, $22/$26, $23/$27, $32/$34, $33/$35, $38/$3A, $39/$3B, $42/$44, $43/$45, $48/$4A, $49/$4B. RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_SwapTilePairs picks entry (wFrameCounterLo & $1F) while that is below 12, and RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_ExchangeTiles swaps the 16 bytes of the two tiles; the routine does nothing once EVENT_SCENE_MONSTER_INSPECTION is set. (C1, E-0381)

02:5254.name: RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_SwapTilePairs7_Data
02:5254.note: Twelve four-byte entries of two little-endian VRAM tile addresses (vTiles2 + 16 * tile number): tiles $33/$35, $34/$36, $42/$44, $43/$45, $4C/$4E, $4D/$4F, $56/$58, $57/$59, $62/$66, $63/$67, $6A/$6E, $6B/$6F. RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_SwapTilePairs7 picks entry (wFrameCounterLo & $1F) while that is below 12 and jumps to RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_ExchangeTiles to swap the two tiles. (C1, E-0381)

02:52A8.name: RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_SwapTilePairsRow0_Data
02:52A8.note: Four four-byte entries of two little-endian VRAM tile addresses (vTiles2 + 16 * tile number): tiles $4E/$50, $4F/$51, $54/$56, $55/$57. RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_SwapTilePairsRow0 picks entry (wFrameCounterLo & $3F) while that is below 4, and only while hMapScreenY is 0, then RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_ExchangeTiles swaps the two tiles. (C1, E-0381)

02:53C5.name: RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_ShiftColourPair_Data
02:53C5.note: Sixteen signed bytes in two halves of eight: 0, -4, -8, -12, -16, -20, -24, -28, then -28, -24, -20, -16, -12, -8, -4, 0. RunFieldEventFieldEventKind_ShiftColourPair adds entry hTemp0 (0-7), plus 8 when bit 0 of wMenuSubState is set, to each 5-bit blue, green and red part of a colour word and floors each part at 0, so the palette cycle of field event 8 darkens the colours and then restores them. (C1, E-0381)

02:5B0A.name: UpdatePlayerMovement_IsTriggerAtCell_Data
02:5B0A.note: Sixteen (X, Y) byte pairs of 16-pixel cell coordinates, sorted by X: (1,2), (1,7), (2,1), (2,4), (2,6), (3,3), (4,5), (4,7), (5,1), (5,3), (6,5), (7,2), (7,4), (7,7), (8,1), (8,6). UpdatePlayerMovement_IsTriggerAtCell indexes it by wTriggerCell (times 2) on key-world maps other than map type $85, and returns 1 when the pair equals the cell (B / 16, C / 16) it is asked about and wTriggerKind is 2 or 3. (C1, E-0381)

02:5B89.name: FieldState_WalkATalks_TalkAtSpotOnDown_Data
02:5B89.note: Five four-byte entries then an $FF end marker: hMapId, a screen byte (hMapScreenX * 16 + hMapScreenY), hPlayerX and hPlayerY of the spot. They are $01/$11/$70/$70, $01/$11/$70/$20, $01/$10/$70/$50, $1A/$10/$70/$70 and $85/$10/$50/$60. FieldState_WalkATalks_TalkAtSpotOnDown walks the list while Down is held and, on a full match, sets wTalkEventGroup to $10 plus the entry index and runs DispatchTalkEvent. (C1, E-0381)

02:64AB.name: FieldState_Still_ChoosePage_DrawCursor_Data
02:64AB.note: Four (column, row) byte pairs in tiles, (1,1), (6,1), (1,3) and (6,3), indexed by the cursor position 0-3 (wMenuState): a 2 by 2 arrangement. FieldState_Still_ChoosePage_DrawCursor adds them to the BG map 0 address of the current scroll position and writes cursor tile $BB (blinking to $C3) at the selected position and tile $C3 at the other three. (C1, E-0381)

02:6835.name: BuildPartyStatusWindowRows_Data
02:6835.note: Three groups of four byte offsets into wWindowTileBuffer + $64 (rows of 20 tiles), one group per party member: level, HP, MP and status mark. Member 0 uses $54, $2B, $3F, $51, member 1 uses $5A, $31, $45, $57 and member 2 uses $60, $37, $4B, $5D, which puts the three members in columns 1, 7 and 13 and the HP, MP and level on rows 2, 3 and 4. BuildPartyStatusWindowRows reads the group of each of the first (wPartyWindowFlags & 3) + 1 entries of wPartyList. (C1, E-0381)

02:6B8C.name: StepTextWindowOpenClose_CopyRow_Data1
02:6B8C.note: One 20-tile window row: $B6, eighteen tiles $C3, $B7 (left edge, blank inside, right edge). StepTextWindowOpenClose_CopyRow (opening) and StepTextWindowOpenClose_CopyRows (closing) copy it with CopyRowsToScreenBufferAndClearAttributes into row 2 of wWindowTileBuffer (+ $28), the middle row of the 20 by 5 text window; it is the first frame of the opening animation and the last of the closing one. (C1, E-0381)

02:6BA0.name: StepTextWindowOpenClose_CopyRow_Data2
02:6BA0.note: Three 20-tile rows of the text window: $B0, eighteen $B1, $B2; then $B6, eighteen $C3, $B7; then $B3, eighteen $B4, $B5 (a box with corner and edge tiles around a blank inside). StepTextWindowOpenClose_CopyRows (opening) and StepTextWindowOpenClose_CopyRow (closing) copy them into rows 1-3 of wWindowTileBuffer (+ $14) with CopyRowsToScreenBufferAndClearAttributes. (C1, E-0381)

02:6BDC.name: StepTextWindowOpenClose_CopyAllRows_Data
02:6BDC.note: The five 20-tile rows of the finished text window: a top edge ($B0, eighteen $B1, $B2); a text row ($B6, tiles $80-$91, $B7); a blank row ($B6, eighteen $C3, $B7); a second text row ($B6, tiles $92-$A3, $B7); a bottom edge ($B3, eighteen $B4, $B5). StepTextWindowOpenClose_CopyAllRows copies them to the start of wWindowTileBuffer when the window opens, then redraws the 20 by 5 area. (C1, E-0381)

02:6DDE.name: WarpEffect_FillScrollTable_Data
02:6DDE.note: Sixteen unsigned wave magnitudes, $00, $60, $B6, $EC, $FF, $EC, $B6, $60 repeated twice (the shape of a sine half-wave scaled to $FF), indexed by e, which starts at (wFrameCounterLo / 4) & $0F and advances by 1 (mod 16) before each pair of lines. WarpEffect_FillScrollTable multiplies the entry by wMenuCursor with Multiply8 and adds the high byte of the product to hScrollX when bit 3 of e is clear, or subtracts it when it is set, for each pair of lines it writes to the line scroll table. (C1, E-0381)

02:6E20.name: WarpEffect_FadePalette_Data
02:6E20.note: Five DMG palette bytes, $D2, $81, $40, $00, $00, indexed by wSubMenuCursor (0-4). WarpEffect_FadePalette stores the entry in wDMGPaletteBGP every frame, so wDMGPaletteBGP steps through those values and ends at $00 (all four colours on shade 0); wSubMenuCursor goes up by 1 every 16 frames and the warp effect moves to its next step when it reaches 4. (C1, E-0381)

02:75F7.name: LoadSaveBlocksFromSRAM_Data
02:75F7.note: Five four-byte entries (address word, length word, both little-endian): $FF8A length $000E (14 bytes of high RAM), $C60C length $0291 (starting at wPlayerName), $CBD7 length $006B (starting at wStoryFlags), $CC42 length $00B5 (starting at wKeyWorldSlot) and an all-zero end entry. LoadSaveBlocksFromSRAM copies each block in turn from sSaveData onward (SRAM bank 1) into RAM, and CopySaveBlocksToSRAMWithSum walks the same list the other way while adding up the bytes. (C1, E-0381)

02:7FFF.name: StartPaletteFade_WhiteColourAddress
02:7FFF.evidence: E-0381 (named from its reading; was StartPaletteFade_SetUpTiming_Data)
02:7FFF.note: The byte stored here, $00, is never read. StartPaletteFade_SetUpTiming loads the ADDRESS of this label into DE (the label sits at $7FFF, the last address of the bank) and writes DE as the colour word to all 32 BG and 32 OBJ palette entries, so the address itself serves as the RGB555 colour $7FFF (white) for a fade in; when bit 7 of wFadeMode is set DE is 0 (black) instead. (C1, E-0381)

03:4DF2.name: ShowSkillNameAtSlotB_Data
03:4DF2.note: Eight VRAM glyph-tile addresses, vTiles2 + $380, + $410, + $4A0, + $530, + $5C0, + $650, + $6E0 and + $770 (steps of $90 = 9 tiles), indexed by the skill slot B (0-7). ShowSkillNameAtSlotB_Skip passes the address with a 9 by 1 window ($0901) to ShowStringBank08AtTilesHL_Bank03, which draws the skill name (category 4) there. (C1, E-0381)

03:4F5D.name: ShowSpeciesNameAndIconForSlotB_Data1
03:4F5D.note: Two VRAM glyph-tile addresses, vTiles2 + $5E0 and vTiles2 + $720 ($95E0, $9720), indexed by the parent slot B (0 or 1). ShowSpeciesNameAndIconForSlotB draws the species name there in a 9 by 1 window (category = species high byte + 2). (C1, E-0381)

03:4F61.name: ShowSpeciesNameAndIconForSlotB_Data2
03:4F61.note: Two VRAM tile numbers, $5D and $71, indexed by the parent slot B (0 or 1). ShowSpeciesNameAndIconForSlotB stores the entry in wWorkBuf + 1 as the tile LoadFamilyIconTileForWorkBuf writes the 16-byte family icon to (the family is in wWorkBuf). (C1, E-0381)

03:518F.name: PauseMenu_Info_PartyOverview_Build_Data1
03:518F.note: Three palette numbers, 1, 3 and 5, indexed by the party slot 0-2. PauseMenu_Info_PartyOverview_Build passes the entry in C to LoadMonsterPicture as the CGB palette slot of that member (two palettes, C and C + 1) and again in hTemp0 as the palette number for LoadMonsterPictureAttributeBlock. (C1, E-0381)

03:5192.name: PauseMenu_Info_PartyOverview_Build_Data2
03:5192.note: Three VRAM destinations, vTiles2 + $140, + $380 and + $5C0 ($9140, $9380, $95C0), indexed by the party slot 0-2. PauseMenu_Info_PartyOverview_Build passes the entry in HL to LoadMonsterPicture, which decompresses the 6 by 6 tile picture of that party member there. (C1, E-0381)

03:5198.name: PauseMenu_Info_PartyOverview_Build_Data3
03:5198.note: Three offsets, $0000, $0080 and $0100, indexed by the party slot 0-2. On CGB PauseMenu_Info_PartyOverview_Build adds $D000 (wScreenAttrBuffer) to the entry and passes it to LoadMonsterPictureAttributeBlock as the place in WRAM bank 2 for the 6 by 6 attribute bytes of that member. (C1, E-0381)

03:519E.name: DrawRecordHPMPAndLevelForRowC_Data
03:519E.note: Three wScreenTileBuffer addresses, $C1FA, $C200 and $C206, indexed by the party slot 0-2 (one column per member). DrawRecordHPMPAndLevelForRowC writes HP as three digit tiles there, MP at +$20 and the level as two digit tiles at +$41. (C1, E-0381)

03:51A4.name: ShowRecordSpeciesNameForRowC_Data
03:51A4.note: Three VRAM glyph-tile addresses, $8800, $8890 and $8920 (vTiles1 + 0, + $90, + $120), indexed by the party slot 0-2. ShowRecordSpeciesNameForRowC uses the entry as the destination of a 9 by 1 text window and draws the species name of that member there. (C1, E-0381)

03:51AA.name: DrawRecordSexMarkTile_Data
03:51AA.note: Three wScreenTileBuffer addresses, $C366, $C386 and $C3A6, indexed by the party slot 0-2. DrawRecordSexMarkTile writes tile $CC + bit 0 of MON_SEX of that member to the address. (C1, E-0381)

03:5264.name: PauseMenu_Info_PartyOverview_Close_LoadTile_Data
03:5264.note: One 8 by 8 tile of 16 bytes in 2-bit graphics format (row pairs): plane 0 is $FF in every row and plane 1 reads $00, $10, $10, $FE, $7C, $38, $7C, $C6, a small star-like figure. PauseMenu_Info_PartyOverview_Close_LoadTile writes it to VRAM tile $14 (vTiles2 + $140), the first tile of the picture area of party member 0 (PauseMenu_Info_PartyOverview_Build_Data2). (C1, E-0381)

03:5C28.name: PersonalityNameTileCounts
03:5C28.evidence: E-0381 (named from its reading; was DrawItemTargetStatPreview_Data)
03:5C28.note: Twenty-seven tile counts, 3 to 9, indexed by the personality number 0-26 of the target monster (PersonalityIndexOfRecord). For an item of kind 2 DrawItemTargetStatPreview shows the personality name (category 7) at vTiles2 + $1A0, then writes that many consecutive tiles from $1A at wWindowTileBuffer + $19 and pads the rest of 9 with the blank tile $C3. (C1, E-0381)

03:6700.name: FieldSkillNumberBySkillId
03:6700.evidence: E-0381 (named from its reading; was LookupInventorySlotForRecordBuffer_Data)
03:6700.note: A table of $B0 bytes, one per skill number, that gives the field skill number or $FF for a skill that cannot be used in the field. SKILL_HEAL to SKILL_REVIVE ($16-$1F, except $20) give 0-9, SKILL_ANTIDOTE ($21) gives $0A, SKILL_CURSEOFF ($24) gives $0B, SKILL_WHISTLE to SKILL_MAPMAGIC ($A2-$A9) give $0C-$13 and every other skill number gives $FF. LookupInventorySlotForRecordBuffer indexes it with the low byte of wRecordBuffer, stores the result in wInventorySlot and returns with Z set when it is $FF. (C1, E-0381)

03:6FBB.name: PauseMenu_Plan_Tactics_ShowCurrent_Data
03:6FBB.note: Three first tile numbers, $D0, $D5 and $DA, indexed by wPauseMenuStep (0-2). PauseMenu_Plan_Tactics_ShowCurrent writes five consecutive tile numbers from the entry to wScreenTileBuffer + $EE and redraws the rectangle at vBGMap0 + $EA. The three runs are $D0-$D4, $D5-$D9 and $DA-$DE. (C1, E-0381)

03:7395.name: PauseMenu_Plan_PagedMenu_WriteFiveTileRun_Data
03:7395.note: Three first tile numbers, $D0, $D5 and $DA (the same bytes as PauseMenu_Plan_Tactics_ShowCurrent_Data), indexed by the party member 0-2 in A. PauseMenu_Plan_PagedMenu_WriteFiveTileRun writes five consecutive tile numbers from the entry at DE; PauseMenu_Plan_PartyOrder_ShowMemberDetails and PauseMenu_Plan_PartyOrder_DrawMemberTiles use it to draw a party member on the party-order screen. (C1, E-0381)

03:78B9.name: PauseMenu_Plan_Keys_DrawKeyNames_Data
03:78B9.note: Five VRAM glyph-tile addresses, vTiles2 + $440, + $500, + $5C0, + $680 and + $740 (steps of $C0 = 12 tiles), indexed by the visible key row c. PauseMenu_Plan_Keys_DrawKeyNames draws the name of each of the four keys of the page in a 12 by 1 text window at the entry for its row; the loop runs rows 0-3 only (rows 1-3 when the list is empty). (C1, E-0381)

03:7BF5.name: GameMode2_Update_OpenPage_Data
03:7BF5.note: Eight bytes read as four RGB555 colours of CGB background palette 1: $2011, $7FFF, $3D7D and $0000. The first six come from the db line and the last two are the first bytes of the zero fill ($00, $00) that follows the label to the end of the bank. GameMode2_Update_OpenPage writes palette 0 inline ($0139, $7FFF, $033F, $0000), then copies these 8 bytes after it, sets wBGPaletteUploadRequest to $7F and calls UploadBGPalettes, only on CGB. (C1, E-0381)

04:48D6.name: UpdateSpriteSlots_FrameLoopType4_Data
04:48D6.note: Seventeen (frame, hold count) byte pairs and an $FF, $FF end marker: frames 0, 3, 4, 5 held $0E, $0A, $0E, $0A frames, repeated once; then frames 0, 1, 2, 1, 2, 0, 6, 7, 6 held $10, $0E, $0E, $0E, $0E, $20, $0E, $20, $0E frames. UpdateSpriteSlots_StepFrameLoop plays the list in a loop for a type 4 sprite slot, storing the current frame in OBJ_SUBINDEX; the object does not move. (C1, E-0381)

04:48FA.name: UpdateSpriteSlots_FrameLoopType5_Data
04:48FA.note: Four (frame, hold count) byte pairs and an $FF, $FF end marker: frames 0, 1, 2, 1, each held $0E frames. UpdateSpriteSlots_StepFrameLoop plays the list in a loop for a type 5 sprite slot, storing the current frame in OBJ_SUBINDEX; the object does not move. (C1, E-0381)

05:614B.name: SlotCHasCastableHealSkill_Data
05:614B.note: Eight bytes, $02, $05, $07, $12, $24, $01, $0C, $1C, read as MP costs. SlotCHasCastableHealSkill takes the cost at index 5, 6 or 7 for SKILL_LIFEDANCE, SKILL_HUSTLE and SKILL_LOVERAIN ($01, $0C, $1C), but for the five heal skills $16-$1A it computes id - $1B, which wraps to $FB-$FF and reads bytes after the table, so entries 0-4 are never indexed by this reader; they look like the costs of the five heal skills ($02, $05, $07, $12, $24). (C1, E-0381)

05:6F6B.name: AnyFoeNotFullyResistant_Data
05:6F6B.note: Twenty-seven (byte offset, field) pairs, indexed by the resistance number RESIST_* (the resistance class minus 1): the byte offset 0-6 inside the seven-byte record of a battle slot in wSlotResistances and the 2-bit field 0-3 in it (field 0 is bits 1-0 ... field 3 is bits 7-6). For example RESIST_BLAZE gives (0, 2), RESIST_VACUUM gives (1, 3) and RESIST_WATERSHOT gives (0, 3). AnyFoeNotFullyResistant, PassIfFoesAverageResistanceAtLeast2, FailIfSkillHasResistanceClass and AIScore_Ramming_LastFoeHPAndResist read the pair and then the field with Get2BitFieldEOfHL. (C1, E-0381)

07:4E07.name: GameMode5_Init_LinkBattleSetup_LoadRules_Data
07:4E07.note: The ten default link rule bytes $01, $00, $00, $63, $29, $01, $00, $00, $63, $80, copied to wLinkRules (which has the single-level limit in +3 = 99, the total level word $0129 = 297 in +4/+5, the family exclusion bits in +6/+7 and wLinkRuleTurnLimit in +8) by GameMode5_Init_LinkBattleSetup_LoadRules unless wLinkSetupMode is 2, in which case wLinkRulesCopy is used. They match the values InitLinkRulesPresetA writes except for the first byte ($01 here, 0 there). (C1, E-0381)

07:5EE3.name: TitleOpening_StartSparkles_Data
07:5EE3.note: Twelve WRAM addresses $D09F, $D0A5, $D0AB, ... $D0E1 (wWorkBuf + 2 + 6 * n), indexed by the sparkle number n kept in wLinkMenuCounter: the start of each six-byte sparkle record. TitleOpening_StartSparkles and TitleOpening_ScrollWithSparkles fetch the word with ReadWordTableEntry_Bank00 and call TitleOpening_InitSparkle on it. wLinkMenuCounter stops at 10, so the last two entries are not reached by these readers. (C1, E-0381)

07:5EFB.name: TitleOpening_MoveSparkles_Data
07:5EFB.note: Four hold times, 4, 7, 7 and 4 frames, indexed by the animation frame (byte 1 of the sparkle record, & 3). TitleOpening_MoveSparkles counts byte 0 of the record up and, once it reaches the hold time, resets it and moves to the next frame; TitleOpening_MoveSparkles_DrawSparkle draws that frame of meta-sprite set $1E at the X (byte 2) and Y (byte 3) of the record. (C1, E-0381)

07:65BD.name: SendLinkByteForMenuOption_Data
07:65BD.note: Eight bytes, $F4, $F4, $FA, $FB, $FC, $DD, $E1, $F3, indexed by the title menu entry wMenuOption & $0F (0-7). SendLinkByteForMenuOption copies the entry to wScreenSubStep and sends it with SerialSendByte, so a linked partner sees which entry is highlighted; entries 0 and 1 (continue and new game) send the same byte $F4. (C1, E-0381)

07:7063.name: LinkRulesEditor_RuleCursor_Data
07:7063.note: Six step numbers of LinkRulesEditor, $03, $0B, $15, $18, $1B, $1E, indexed by the rule row wMenuSubState & 7. When A is pressed LinkRulesEditor_RuleCursor stores the entry in wTitleScreenSubState, which selects the steps LinkRulesEditor_DecideRule, LinkRulesEditor_YesNoRule, LinkRulesEditor_YesNoRule2, LinkRulesEditor_YesNoRule3, LinkRulesEditor_YesNoRule4 and LinkRulesEditor_FifthRule in turn. (C1, E-0381)

07:7700.name: LinkRulesEditor_ToggleFamily_MoveCursor_Data
07:7700.note: Eleven BG map addresses, $9943, $9945, ... $994D (vBGMap0 row 10, columns 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13) and $9983, $9985, ... $998B (row 12, columns 3-11), indexed by the family cursor wMenuCursor (0-10). LinkRulesEditor_ToggleFamily_MoveCursor blinks the cursor tile at the address of the selected family; Up and Down move between the two rows. (C1, E-0381)

07:774D.name: LinkRulesEditor_ToggleFamily_FlipExclusion_Data
07:774D.note: Eleven (byte offset, bit mask) pairs, indexed by the family number 0-10: families 0-6 are bits $40, $20, $10, $08, $04, $02, $01 of wLinkRules + 6 and families 7-10 are bits $80, $40, $20, $10 of wLinkRules + 7. LinkRulesEditor_ToggleFamily_FlipExclusion flips the bit for the family under the cursor, and LinkRulesEditor_DrawFamilyMark tests it (set = family excluded, blank tile $C3 drawn instead of the family tile). (C1, E-0381)

07:7BFD.name: DrawWorkBufSelectionTilesAndPanels_LevelRule_Data1
07:7BFD.note: Five tile numbers, $15, $12, $15, $0B, $10: the label of the total-level rule on the rules summary. DrawWorkBufSelectionTilesAndPanels_LevelRule copies them to wScreenTileBuffer + $126 when bit 6 of wLinkRules + 5 is clear, followed by the number (wLinkRules + 5 bit 0) * 256 + wLinkRules + 4. (C1, E-0381)

07:7C02.name: DrawWorkBufSelectionTilesAndPanels_LevelRule_Data2
07:7C02.note: Five tile numbers, $29, $0B, $16, $C3, $C3 (two blank tiles at the end): the label of the single-level limit rule on the rules summary. DrawWorkBufSelectionTilesAndPanels_LevelRule copies them to wScreenTileBuffer + $126 when bit 6 of wLinkRules + 5 is set, followed by the number wLinkRules + 3. (C1, E-0381)

08:4038.name: StringDatabase_MonsterNames2
08:4038.evidence: E-0381 (named from its reading; was CopyNameStringFromBank08Database_Data1)
08:4038.note: This is not a table of its own but the word at StringDatabase + 6, the category 3 entry (StringTable_MonsterNames2). CopyNameStringFromBank08Database (bank $F0) loads its address into DE and reads the word from bank $08 with ReadFarPointerAtDEInBankB to get the string list, then adds twice the name index in the record to find the string; it uses this address when the byte after the index is non-zero, and the category 2 address when that byte is 0. (C1, E-0381)

08:403C.name: StringDatabase_ItemNames
08:403C.note: This is not a table of its own but the word at StringDatabase + 10, the category 5 entry (StringTable_ItemNames). ArenaMenu_PickPrize_GiveItem_CopyName loads its address into DE, reads the string list pointer from bank $08 with ReadFarPointerAtDEInBankB, adds twice wArg1 (the item number) to find the name string and copies it to wTextBuf1 up to the $F0 end. (C1, E-0381)

0A:4374.name: EnterStatusEffectFieldState_Data
0A:4374.note: A list of 64 map ids in ascending order apart from $B2, $B1, then an $FF end marker: $21-$26, $29-$2B, $2D, $2E, $31-$34, $3C, $3D, $41, $45, $49-$4D, $4F-$52, $58-$61, $68, $71, $72, $78, $79, $7C-$7F, $89, $92, $9D, $A4, $A9, $AB, $AF, $B2, $B1, $B6, $B9, $BA, $BC, $C5, $D0, $D9, $E2. EnterStatusEffectFieldState compares hMapId with each byte (outside key worlds, on maps $20 and above) and returns at once on a match, so none of the poison and MP-drain field steps run on those maps. (C1, E-0381)

0A:46EE.name: RunBattleIntroKindCase_KeyWorldStrength_Data1
0A:46EE.note: Twenty little-endian words, indexed by party strength / 5 (wPartyStrength, quotient from DivideBByA): base monster numbers $00AC, $00BC, $00CC, $00DC, $00EC, $00FC, $010C, $011C, $012C, $013C, then $021E, $0223, $0228, $022D, $0232, $0237, $023C, $0241, $0246, $0248. RunBattleIntroKindCase_KeyWorldStrength stores the word in hTemp0/hTemp1 and gives each of the three foes in wEncounterMonsters that number plus a random 0-9. (C1, E-0381)

0A:4716.name: RunBattleIntroKindCase_KeyWorldStrength_Data2
0A:4716.note: Twelve little-endian monster numbers in four groups of three, one group per field event $0C-$0F: $020B, $020C, $020D; $020E, $020F, $020E; $0210, $0211, $0212; $0213, $0214, $0215. RunBattleIntroKindCase_KeyWorldStrength copies the group 6 * (wPendingFieldEvent & $0F - $0C) bytes in to wEncounterMonsters as the three fixed foes of that event. (C1, E-0381)

0A:478F.name: PickRandomEncounterCountdownFromTable_Data
0A:478F.note: Twenty-one counts in ascending order: $0A, $14, $19, $1E, $23, $28, $2A, $2C, $2D, $2E, $30, $32, $34, $36, $38, $3A, $3C, $41, $46, $50, $50. PickRandomEncounterCountdownFromTable indexes it by (wKeyRandomHi & $3F) / 5, which is at most 12, and stores twice the entry in wEncounterCountdown, so only the first 13 entries are reached. (C1, E-0381)

0A:514C.name: FillEncounterFromEntry_Data1
0A:514C.note: Four encounter kind values, 0, 2, 1, 2, indexed by wRandomLo & 3 after NextTableByte. FillEncounterFromEntry replaces an encounter kind of 2 or more with the entry, and RunBattleIntroKindCase_KeyWorldEncounter picks wEncounterKind from it at random (kind 2 twice as often as 0 or 1). (C1, E-0381)

0A:5150.name: FillEncounterFromEntry_Data2
0A:5150.note: Four encounter kind values, 0, 1, 0, 1, indexed by wRandomLo & 3 after NextTableByte. FillEncounterFromEntry replaces an encounter kind of exactly 1 with the entry, so such an entry becomes kind 0 or 1 at random. (C1, E-0381)

0A:55FA.name: StripeTransition_BlankStripes_Data1
0A:55FA.note: Nine widths in tiles, 20, 18, 16, 14, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, indexed by the stage wTransitionStage (0-8). StripeTransition_BlankStripes blanks one rectangular ring of tiles per stage, outermost first, with this width for the top and bottom edges (StripeTransition_BlankStripes_Data2 gives the height); the first ring is the whole 20 tile wide screen. (C1, E-0381)

0A:5603.name: StripeTransition_BlankStripes_Data2
0A:5603.note: Nine heights in tiles, 18, 16, 14, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, indexed by the stage wTransitionStage (0-8). StripeTransition_BlankStripes blanks the left and right edges of the ring of that stage with this height, in steps of one BG map row ($20); with StripeTransition_BlankStripes_Data1 the rings shrink by 2 tiles in each direction per stage. (C1, E-0381)

0C:4331.name: LibraryMenu_FamilyCursor_DrawTile_Data
0C:4331.note: Six little-endian offsets, $0021, $0061, $00A1, $00E1, $0121, $0161 (BG map row 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 at column 1), indexed by wGridCursorX (0-5). LibraryMenu_FamilyCursor_DrawTile adds the entry to the BG map 0 address of the scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank0C) and writes the tile in B there, which draws or erases the family cursor. (C1, E-0381)

0C:45FD.name: LibraryMenu_MonsterCursor_DrawTile_Data
0C:45FD.note: Six little-endian offsets, $0029, $0069, $00A9, $00E9, $0129, $0169 (BG map row 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 at column 9), indexed by wGrid2CursorX (0-5). LibraryMenu_MonsterCursor_DrawTile adds the entry to the BG map 0 address of the scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank0C) and writes the tile in B there, which draws or erases the monster cursor. (C1, E-0381)

0C:4AA0.name: LibraryMenu_ShowMonsterEntry_DrawEntry_Data
0C:4AA0.note: Three VRAM glyph-tile addresses, vTiles2 + $440, + $4D0 and + $560 ($9440, $94D0, $9560), indexed by the skill row c (0-2). LibraryMenu_ShowMonsterEntry_DrawEntry uses each as the 9 by 1 text window where ShowString_Bank08 draws the skill name (category 4) of the skill number at wArg5 + c after LoadSpeciesBytes8To10ToArg5 and PermuteArg5To7ByMonster. (C1, E-0381)

0C:4F68.name: LibraryMenu_DrawSeenNames_Data
0C:4F68.note: Six VRAM glyph-tile addresses, vTiles2 + $200, + $290, + $320, + $3B0, + $440 and + $4D0 (steps of $90 = 9 tiles), indexed by the row c (0-5) of the page of the monster list. LibraryMenu_DrawSeenNames uses each as the 9 by 1 text window where it draws the name of a seen monster (ShowString_Bank08) or the placeholder string 0 of bank $0B (ShowString_Bank0B). (C1, E-0381)

0C:4FAA.name: LibraryMenu_LoadFamilyIcons_Data
0C:4FAA.note: The first 12 bytes are two rows of six family numbers for the family grid, indexed by 6 * wGridCursorY + c: row 0 holds families $00-$05 and row 1 holds $06-$0A and $FF (no family). LibraryMenu_LoadFamilyIcons skips $FF and, for the others, calls LoadFamilyIconTileForWorkBuf with the family number in wWorkBuf and the tile number (family mod 6) + 2 in wWorkBuf + 1. The last 12 bytes are six words, vTiles2 + $20, + $70, + $C0, + $110, + $160 and + $1B0, that this reader never indexes. (C1, E-0381)

0C:5103.name: LibraryMenu_DrawSeenCounts_Data1
0C:5103.note: Six little-endian offsets, $0026, $0066, $00A6, $00E6, $0126, $0166 (BG map row 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 at column 6), indexed by the row c of the family row. LibraryMenu_DrawSeenCounts adds the entry to the BG map 0 address of the scroll position to place the two digit tiles of the seen count when wArg1 is 0. (C1, E-0381)

0C:510F.name: LibraryMenu_DrawSeenCounts_Data2
0C:510F.note: Six wWindowTileBuffer addresses, $C37E, $C3A6, $C3CE, $C3F6, $C41E, $C446 (rows 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16 at column 6 of the 20-tile-wide buffer), indexed by the row c. LibraryMenu_DrawSeenCounts writes the two digit tiles of the seen count there instead of to the BG map when wArg1 is non-zero. (C1, E-0381)

0C:5513.name: LibraryMenu_ShowMonsterEntry_LoadClassBlock_Data
0C:5513.note: Eight pointers, one per class 0-7, to the eight 4-byte tile rows LibraryClassBlock_Class0 to LibraryClassBlock_Class7. LibraryMenu_ShowMonsterEntry_LoadClassBlock takes the class byte of the shown monster from LibraryMonsterClasses, doubles it to pick the word, and copies the 4 tiles it points at to wLibraryEntryBlock. (C1, E-0381)

0C:555C.name: WriteBGPalette0FromData_Data
0C:555C.note: Three CGB colours as little-endian BGR555 words: $7D86, $7FFF (white) and $7FE1. WriteBGPalette0FromData writes the six bytes in order through rBGPD starting at palette index 0, so they become colours 0 to 2 of background palette 0 (colour 3 is not written). (C1, E-0381)

0C:68D1.name: ArenaMenu_ClassCursor_Data1
0C:68D1.note: Four text characters, "C", "B", "A" and "S" in the charmap ($0C, $0B, $0A, $1C): the arena class letters. ArenaMenu_ClassCursor indexes it with wGridCursorX (0-3, the class under the cursor) and stores the letter in wTextBuf0, followed by the $F0 terminator, so the next message can show it with <BUF0>. (C1, E-0381)

0C:691A.name: ArenaMenu_ClassCursor_DrawTile_Data
0C:691A.note: Four little-endian word offsets into the BG map, counted from the BG map address of the screen scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank0C): $00A2, $00E2, $0122 and $0162, which are rows 5, 7, 9 and 11 at column 2. ArenaMenu_ClassCursor_DrawTile indexes it with wGridCursorX (0-3) to put the cursor tile B beside the class row. (C1, E-0381)

0C:6C7F.name: ArenaMenu_ClassCursor2_Data1
0C:6C7F.note: Four text characters, "C", "B", "A" and "S" ($0C, $0B, $0A, $1C): the arena class letters for the second class panel, the same bytes as ArenaMenu_ClassCursor_Data1. ArenaMenu_ClassCursor2 indexes it with wGridCursorX (0-3) and stores the letter in wTextBuf0 with the $F0 terminator, for <BUF0> in the next message. (C1, E-0381)

0C:6CC8.name: ArenaMenu_ClassCursor2_DrawTile_Data
0C:6CC8.note: Four little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank0C): $00A1, $00E1, $0121 and $0161, which are rows 5, 7, 9 and 11 at column 1. ArenaMenu_ClassCursor2_DrawTile indexes it with wGridCursorX (0-3) to draw the cursor tile B for the second class panel; the values are those of ArenaMenu_ClassCursor_DrawTile_Data one column to the left. (C1, E-0381)

0C:6D44.name: ArenaMenu_SetClassFee_Data
0C:6D44.note: Four little-endian 16-bit amounts: 1000, 2000, 3000 and 5000 ($03E8, $07D0, $0BB8, $1388). ArenaMenu_SetClassFee indexes it with wGridCursorX (the class chosen, 0-3) times 2 and stores the word in wArenaFeeLo and wArenaFeeHi, the entry fee that is later taken from the gold. (C1, E-0381)

0C:7037.name: ArenaMenu_PrepareResultName_ClassLetter_Data
0C:7037.note: Six text characters, "C", "C", "C", "B", "A", "S" ($0C, $0C, $0C, $0B, $0A, $1C), one per wAreaGraphicsIndex 0-5. ArenaMenu_PrepareResultName_ClassLetter stores the letter in wTextBuf0 with a $F0 terminator after it. Areas 0-2 share the letter C; 3, 4 and 5 give B, A and S. (C1, E-0381)

0C:72C0.name: PickTableEntryByPartyLevelTotal_Data
0C:72C0.note: Six little-endian words: 400, 600, 800, 1200, 1400 and 1400 ($0190, $0258, $0320, $04B0, $0578, $0578). PickTableEntryByPartyLevelTotal adds the MON_LEVEL of every party member and picks the word by the total: entry 0 below 49, 1 below 91, 2 below 139, 3 below 181, 4 below 220 and 5 from 220 up (also for totals of 256 or more); it returns the word in HL. (C1, E-0381)

0C:7538.name: ArenaMenu_PickPrize_RandomItem_Data
0C:7538.note: Four word pointers (8 bytes) followed by four lists of 7 item ids each: $40-$46, $47-$4D, $4E-$53 with $5A, and $5B-$61. ArenaMenu_PickPrize_RandomItem takes the roll from RandomModulo52, uses its low two bits to choose the list, then the roll modulo 7 to choose an item id, which it leaves in wArg1 for ArenaMenu_PickPrize_GiveItem. (C1, E-0381)

0C:75D2.name: ArenaMenu_PickPrize_Data1
0C:75D2.note: Six word pointers (areas 0-2 share the first list, wAreaGraphicsIndex selects the word) followed by four lists of 9 bytes: eight ascending thresholds ending in $64, then an $FF end mark; the first list is 25, 35, 45, 55, 65, 75, 95, 100. ArenaMenu_PickPrize rolls 0-96 with RandomModulo52 and walks the list to the first threshold that is at least the roll; that position (0-7) indexes the matching list of ArenaMenu_PickPrize_Data2, and reaching the $FF would give gold instead. (C1, E-0381)

0C:7602.name: ArenaMenu_PickPrize_Data2
0C:7602.note: Six word pointers (areas 0-2 share the first list) followed by four lists of 8 outcome bytes, indexed by the position ArenaMenu_PickPrize found in ArenaMenu_PickPrize_Data1. $FE tries GenerateNewKeyEntry (6000 gold is given instead when it makes no key), $FD draws an item through ArenaMenu_PickPrize_RandomItem, and any other byte is an item id in wArg1 handed to ArenaMenu_PickPrize_GiveItem; the first list is ITEM_HERB, ITEM_DSCALE, ITEM_ELFWATER, ITEM_WORLDLEAF, ITEM_WIND, ITEM_SAGEROCK, ITEM_SIRLOIN, ITEM_STONEFANG. (C1, E-0381)

0D:49FD.name: EggServiceMenu_Appraise_RateStats_Data
0D:49FD.note: Six MON record offsets, each a word: $5D MON_MAX_HP, $61 MON_MAX_MP, $63 MON_ATK, $65 MON_DEF, $67 MON_AGL and $69 MON_INT. EggServiceMenu_Appraise_RateStats loads each word from the egg record, adds them, divides by 6 and rates the average: under 51 gives 0, under 101 gives 1, under 201 gives 2 and 201 or more gives 3, stored in wTwoChoiceCursor to pick the appraisal message. (C1, E-0381)

0D:4DC7.name: DrawTileAtChoiceCursor_Data
0D:4DC7.note: Two little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank0D): $012D and $016D, which are row 9 and row 11 at column 13. DrawTileAtChoiceCursor indexes it with wChoiceCursor times 2 and writes the tile B there, the marker beside the choice. (C1, E-0381)

0D:5504.name: RenameMenu_PartyCursor_DrawTile_Data
0D:5504.note: Three little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank0D): $0061, $00A1 and $00E1, which are rows 3, 5 and 7 at column 1. RenameMenu_PartyCursor_DrawTile indexes it with wGridCursorX times 2 and writes the tile B there, the renaming cursor. (C1, E-0381)

0D:5D0E.name: EraseCursorForArg5Layout_Data1
0D:5D0E.note: Four little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position: $00A6, $00C6, $00E6 and $0106, rows 5 to 8 at column 6. EraseCursorForArg5Layout uses this layout when wArg5 is 0 and indexes it with wListCursor times 2, to write the blank tile $C3 over the cursor of that list row. (C1, E-0381)

0D:5D16.name: EraseCursorForArg5Layout_Data2
0D:5D16.note: Four little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position: $00A4, $00C4, $00E4 and $0104, rows 5 to 8 at column 4. EraseCursorForArg5Layout uses this layout when wArg5 is 1 and indexes it with wListCursor times 2 to write the blank tile $C3 over the list cursor. (C1, E-0381)

0D:5D1E.name: EraseCursorForArg5Layout_Data3
0D:5D1E.note: Four little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position: $00A2, $00C2, $00E2 and $0102, rows 5 to 8 at column 2. EraseCursorForArg5Layout uses this layout when wArg5 is neither 0 nor 1 and indexes it with wListCursor times 2 to write the blank tile $C3 over the list cursor. (C1, E-0381)

0D:5DDD.name: DrawKeyListPageMarks_Data1
0D:5DDD.note: Four little-endian addresses inside wWindowTileBuffer (20 tiles per row): $C3CD, $C3F5, $C41D and $C445, which are rows 10, 12, 14 and 16 at column 5, one per key slot on a page. DrawKeyListPageMarks uses them when wArg5 is 0: it first writes the blank tile $C3 to all four, then for key slot c of the page writes $CA (a key with bit 6 set) or $C3 at entry c. (C1, E-0381)

0D:5DE5.name: DrawKeyListPageMarks_Data2
0D:5DE5.note: Four little-endian addresses inside wWindowTileBuffer (20 tiles per row): $C3C9, $C3F1, $C419 and $C441, rows 10, 12, 14 and 16 at column 1. DrawKeyListPageMarks uses this set when wArg5 is non-zero: it blanks all four with $C3, then for key slot c of the page writes $70 (a key with bit 6 set) or $C3 at entry c. (C1, E-0381)

0D:6D06.name: MedalPrizeMenu_FindFreeRecord_Data
0D:6D06.note: Three bytes, 10, 20 and 30: the number of SRAM monster record slots (sRecords, $A5 bytes each) MedalPrizeMenu_FindFreeRecord looks through, picked by wFarmLevel. The routine stops at the first slot whose first byte is 0 or $FF and returns $FF when none of that many slots is free. (C1, E-0381)

0D:6D9F.name: MedalPrizeMenu_DrawPrices_Data
0D:6D9F.note: Four little-endian addresses inside wWindowTileBuffer: $C3D7, $C3FF, $C427 and $C44F, which are rows 10, 12, 14 and 16 at column 15. MedalPrizeMenu_DrawPrices writes the two digit tiles (tens, ones) of the medal price of prize c of the page at the address of entry c, for up to four prizes a page. (C1, E-0381)

0D:6DC8.name: WriteTileBAtCursorListCursor_Data
0D:6DC8.note: Four little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank0D): $00A4, $00E4, $0124 and $0164, which are rows 5, 7, 9 and 11 at column 4. WriteTileBAtCursorListCursor indexes it with wListCursor times 2 and writes the tile B at that position. (C1, E-0381)

0D:7499.name: NpcBreedMenu_ChooseAndBreed_ReplaceParent_Data
0D:7499.note: Ten little-endian word story flag numbers: $010E, $0118, $011A, $0125 and $0129 (EVENT_WHEN_YOU_BREED_THE_OFFSPRING, EVENT_BREEDING_COULD_RESULT_IN, EVENT_IF_YOU_GET_AN, EVENT_BREEDING_COULD_RESULT_IN_125, EVENT_ALL_RIGHTY_WELL_DO), then $0032 to $0036 (EVENT_WHEN_YOU_BREED_MONSTERS, EVENT_WHEN_YOU_BREED_MONSTERS_033, EVENT_WHEN_YOU_BREED_MONSTERS_034, EVENT_BREEDING_FIRE_AND_ICE, EVENT_BREEDING_FIRE_AND_ICE_036). NpcBreedMenu_ChooseAndBreed_ReplaceParent indexes it with wScreenTableIndex times 2 and sets that flag with SetFlagBit after it stores the child record. (C1, E-0381)

0D:75D7.name: NpcBreedMenu_RedrawListScreen_LoadTiles_Data1
0D:75D7.note: Sixteen 3-byte far pointers (address low, address high, bank), indexed by wScreenTableIndex times 3. Each points at a compressed map tile set in bank $48: Map04Tileset ($6B82) for indexes 0, 2, 4 and 8-15, and Map17Tileset ($49A9) for 1, 3, 5, 6 and 7. NpcBreedMenu_RedrawListScreen_LoadTiles decompresses the chosen one to vTiles2 with DecompressToVRAM. (C1, E-0381)

0D:7607.name: NpcBreedMenu_RedrawListScreen_LoadTiles_Data2
0D:7607.note: Sixteen 3-byte far pointers (address low, address high, bank), indexed by wScreenTableIndex times 3, to 64-byte palettes in bank $48: Map04Palettes ($6F34) for indexes 0, 2, 4 and 8-15, and Map17Palettes ($4C87) for 1, 3, 5, 6 and 7. It pairs entry for entry with NpcBreedMenu_RedrawListScreen_LoadTiles_Data1; NpcBreedMenu_RedrawListScreen_LoadTiles copies the 64 bytes to wBGPaletteBuffer with CopyFromBankWaitVRAM. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5A6B.name: AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data1
0E:5A6B.note: Eight word pointers, one per stat index c = 0-7 in the order of the child record stat words from MON_HP: HP, max HP, MP, max MP, ATK, DEF, AGL and INT. Each points at a list of MON_ITEM values ending in $FF (the _Entry00 to _Entry07 labels below; stats 0-1 share one list and stats 2-3 share another). AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems searches the list of stat c for the MON_ITEM of each parent record. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5A7B.name: AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data1_Entry00
0E:5A7B.note: The $FF-terminated list of MON_ITEM values $01 and $02, the items that matter for stat indexes 0 and 1 (HP and max HP). When a parent record MON_ITEM is in the list, AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems subtracts the amount AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data2 gives for that item from the parent stat word. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5A7E.name: AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data1_Entry02
0E:5A7E.note: The $FF-terminated list of MON_ITEM values $03 and $04, the items that matter for stat indexes 2 and 3 (MP and max MP). A parent MON_ITEM in the list makes AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems subtract that item amount from AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data2 from the parent stat word. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5A81.name: AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data1_Entry04
0E:5A81.note: The $FF-terminated list of MON_ITEM values $05 and $06, the items that matter for stat index 4 (ATK). A parent MON_ITEM in the list makes AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems subtract that item amount from AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data2 from the parent ATK word. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5A84.name: AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data1_Entry05
0E:5A84.note: The $FF-terminated list of MON_ITEM values $07, $08 and $14, the items that matter for stat index 5 (DEF). A parent MON_ITEM in the list makes AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems subtract that item amount from AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data2 from the parent DEF word. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5A88.name: AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data1_Entry06
0E:5A88.note: The $FF-terminated list of MON_ITEM values $09 and $0A, the items that matter for stat index 6 (AGL). A parent MON_ITEM in the list makes AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems subtract that item amount from AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data2 from the parent AGL word. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5A8B.name: AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data1_Entry07
0E:5A8B.note: The $FF-terminated list of MON_ITEM values $0B and $0C, the items that matter for stat index 7 (INT). A parent MON_ITEM in the list makes AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems subtract that item amount from AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data2 from the parent INT word. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5A8E.name: AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems_Data2
0E:5A8E.note: Twenty-two bytes indexed by a MON_ITEM value (0-$15): the amount subtracted from a parent stat word. Non-zero entries are item 1 = 30, 2 = 80, 3 = 30, 4 = 80, 5 = 10, 6 = 50, 7 = 10, 8 = 50, 9 = 10, $A = 50, $B = 50, $C = 100 and $14 = 5; all others are 0. AdjustStatForRecordBufAAndBItems subtracts it (16-bit, no floor at 0) unless the stat is already 999 or more. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5E02.name: TestResistanceEntry_Data
0E:5E02.note: 27 bytes indexed by MON_ITEM - 1 (items 1 to $1B): each is a resistance index 0-$1A, and together they use every index once (the order starts 0-6, then $0E, $0F, 7, $10-$14, 8-$B and so on). TestResistanceEntry returns $FF instead of level 2 for resistance C when the record MON_ITEM is 1-$1B and this table byte equals C; SumRecordBufAAndBResistanceTests uses it for both parents. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5E61.name: CopySixBytesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data1
0E:5E61.note: Six little-endian addresses in the breeding record buffers, the sources used when bit 4 of the child MON_FAMILY is clear: wRecordBufA + MON_SPECIES (two bytes, $C991 and $C992), wRecordBufB + MON_SPECIES ($CA36, $CA37), then the MON_PLUS bytes of wRecordBufA ($C9F3) and of wRecordBufB ($CA98). CopySixBytesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table copies byte i from these to the destination in CopySixBytesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data3. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5E6D.name: CopySixBytesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data2
0E:5E6D.note: The same six source addresses as CopySixBytesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data1 with parent A and parent B swapped ($CA36, $CA37, $C991, $C992, then the MON_PLUS bytes $CA98 and $C9F3), used when bit 4 of the child MON_FAMILY is set. CopySixBytesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table copies byte i from these to the destination in CopySixBytesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data3. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5E79.name: CopySixBytesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data3
0E:5E79.note: Six little-endian destination addresses in wChildRecord: $CAEA to $CAED (MON_PARENT1_SPECIES and MON_PARENT2_SPECIES, two bytes each), $CB68 (MON_PARENT1_PLUS) and $CB73 (MON_PARENT2_PLUS). CopySixBytesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table stores source byte i to entry i whichever source table it used. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5ED0.name: CopyFourNamesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data1
0E:5ED0.note: Four little-endian source addresses used when bit 4 of the child MON_FAMILY is clear: wRecordBufA + MON_NAME ($C987), wRecordBufB + MON_NAME ($CA2C), wRecordBufA + MON_MASTER_NAME ($C995) and wRecordBufB + MON_MASTER_NAME ($CA3A). CopyFourNamesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table copies 10 bytes from entry i to the destination of entry i in CopyFourNamesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data3. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5ED8.name: CopyFourNamesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data2
0E:5ED8.note: The same four source addresses as CopyFourNamesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data1 with parent A and B swapped ($CA2C, $C987, $CA3A, $C995), used when bit 4 of the child MON_FAMILY is set. CopyFourNamesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table copies 10 bytes from entry i to the destination of entry i in CopyFourNamesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data3. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5EE0.name: CopyFourNamesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table_Data3
0E:5EE0.note: Four little-endian destination addresses in wChildRecord: $CB5E (MON_PARENT1_NAME), $CB69 (MON_PARENT2_NAME), $CAEE (MON_PARENT1_MASTER) and $CAF9 (MON_PARENT2_MASTER). CopyFourNamesByChildRecordFamilyBit4Table copies a 10-byte name from the source of entry i to entry i whichever source table it used. (C1, E-0381)

0E:5F89.name: ApplyBreedingBonusToChildStats_Data
0E:5F89.note: Eight MON record offsets, each a stat word of wChildRecord: $5B MON_HP, $5D MON_MAX_HP, $5F MON_MP, $61 MON_MAX_MP, $63 MON_ATK, $65 MON_DEF, $67 MON_AGL and $69 MON_INT. ApplyBreedingBonusToChildStats walks the list and adds word * bonus / 100 (rounded up, capped at 999) to each. (C1, E-0381)

0F:40DE.name: PersonalityMessage_PickMessage_Data
0F:40DE.note: Eleven message numbers, one per family 0-10 (the low nibble of MON_FAMILY): $94, $AF, $CA, $AF, $94, $CA, $AF, $94, $CA, $CA and $E5. PersonalityMessage_PickMessage adds the personality index of the follower (PersonalityIndexOfRecord, 0-26) to the byte and starts the result as a message of group 5, so each value is the first of 27 consecutive messages. (C1, E-0381)

0F:431F.name: SceneHomecoming_MoveBack_Data
0F:431F.note: 64 signed bytes ($00, $01 or $FF for -1): the X step added each frame to object 2, the player and the scene object, indexed by wScriptParam0 (the frame count 0-$3F). Step 28 (SceneHomecoming_MoveTogether) adds them as they are and step 29 (SceneHomecoming_MoveBack) adds the negated value, so the group returns to its start X: the 64 values sum to 0, and the running total in step 28 stays between 0 and +7 (step 29 mirrors it). (C1, E-0381)

0F:6D78.name: SceneKamehaFlees_BobObjectRight_Data
0F:6D78.note: Eight Y positions for the scene object (SCRIPTOBJ_Y): 64, 63, 64, 63, 64, 62, 64, 65 ($40, $3F, $40, $3F, $40, $3E, $40, $41). SceneKamehaFlees_BobObjectRight advances wScriptParam0 by 1 each frame modulo 8, so the object bobs about the row of $40 while it moves right. (C1, E-0381)

10:4AFF.name: StartMessageForGroup_Data
10:4AFF.note: Eleven 3-byte far pointers (address low, address high, bank), indexed by wMessageMode - 1: the per-mode begin-message routines BeginStringDisplay_BankF0 (modes 1 and 2), BeginStringDisplay_Bank1F, BeginStringDisplay_Bank1D, BeginBreedingStringDisplay, BeginStringDisplay_BankF2, BeginStringDisplay_Bank0D, BeginMessageDisplay_Bank0E, BeginStringDisplay_Bank0B, BeginStringDisplay_Bank33 and BeginStringDisplay_Bank24. StartMessageForGroup calls the chosen one through rst $10 with wStringCategory 0 and wStringIndex = the message L. (C1, E-0381)

11:42AC.name: WarpToLinkedMapForCurrentMap_Data1
11:42AC.note: Eleven map ids in ascending order, $29, $45, $68, $9D, $A4, $AF, $B2, $C5, $D0, $D9 and $E2, ended by $FF: the maps WarpToLinkedMapForCurrentMap looks hMapId up in. The position N where hMapId is found indexes the 3-byte records of WarpToLinkedMapForCurrentMap_Data2. The ids are the same as CheckMapExitEntry_Data. (C1, E-0381)

11:42B8.name: WarpToLinkedMapForCurrentMap_Data2
11:42B8.note: Eleven 3-byte records, entry N for the N-th map of WarpToLinkedMapForCurrentMap_Data1: the new hMapId ($20, $30, $48, $70, $A0, $A8, $B0, $B8, $C8, $D1, $DA), a position byte (always $44; high nibble the destination X, low nibble Y, each times 16) and a screen byte (high nibble hMapScreenX, low nibble hMapScreenY: $00, $76, $B4, $B4, $10, $00, $01, $44, $01, $00, $00). WarpToLinkedMapForCurrentMap_StartWarp reads the last two bytes; a key world with wKeyWorldKey - 1 = N uses wKeyWorldGoal for them. The same records, with a link number added, make CheckMapExitTable_Data. (C1, E-0381)

11:4480.name: CheckMapExitTable_Data
11:4480.note: Eleven 4-byte records and an $FF end mark: map id ($20, $30, $48, $70, $A0, $A8, $B0, $B8, $C8, $D1, $DA, ascending), a position byte (always $44: the player X cell in the high nibble, the Y cell in the low, cells of 16 pixels), a screen byte (hMapScreenX in the high nibble, hMapScreenY in the low: $00, $76, $B4, $B4, $10, $00, $01, $44, $01, $00, $00) and a link number 1-11. CheckMapExitTable finds the record of hMapId and CheckMapExitEntry warps when the player stands on that position and screen, to the map CheckMapExitEntry_Data gives for link number - 1. (C1, E-0381)

11:44AD.name: CheckMapExitEntry_Data
11:44AD.note: Eleven destination map ids, $29, $45, $68, $9D, $A4, $AF, $B2, $C5, $D0, $D9 and $E2, indexed by the link number (1-11) of a CheckMapExitTable_Data record minus 1. CheckMapExitEntry loads the chosen id into hMapId and warps to screen (0,0) at ($40,$80). The values are the same as WarpToLinkedMapForCurrentMap_Data1, the maps that link back. (C1, E-0381)

12:5E62.name: FieldScene01_DrawSprite_Data
12:5E62.note: A $FF-terminated list of map ids holding one id, $30 (then $FF). FieldScene01_DrawSprite searches it for hMapId on a map that is not a special map; on a match, or in a key world of map type $80, it queues music $2B with QueueMusic. (C1, E-0381)

12:6B7A.name: DrawAnimatedMetaSprite1B_Data
12:6B7A.note: 30 bytes of sprite sub-index for the animated meta-sprite set $1B: ten $00, ten $01 and ten $02. DrawAnimatedMetaSprite1B indexes it with the frame counter (wFrameCounterLo and wFrameCounterHi) modulo 30 and stores the byte in hSpriteSubIndex, so the sprite cycles through three sub-sprites, each shown for 10 frames. (C1, E-0381)

12:6FF2.name: DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex_Data1
12:6FF2.note: A list of frame durations in frames, 8, 8, 8, 8, ended by $FF: four frames of 8 frames each, for sprite set $13. DrawFieldSprites_StepFrameLoop counts wObject5 + $6 up to the duration of frame wObject5 + $7, then advances the frame, wrapping to 0 when the next entry is $FF; the frame number is the sub-index (hSpriteSubIndex). (C1, E-0381)

12:6FF7.name: DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex_Data2
12:6FF7.note: A list of frame durations, 8, 8, ended by $FF: two frames of 8 frames each, for sprite set $1A. DrawFieldSprites_StepFrameLoop advances the frame in wObject5 + $7 when the counter wObject5 + $6 reaches the current duration and wraps to frame 0 at the $FF; the frame number is the sub-index. (C1, E-0381)

12:6FFA.name: DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex_Data3
12:6FFA.note: A list of frame durations, 7, 7, 9, ended by $FF: three frames for sprite set $17. DrawFieldSprites_StepFrameLoop advances the frame in wObject5 + $7 when the counter wObject5 + $6 reaches the current duration and wraps to frame 0 at the $FF; the frame number is the sub-index. (C1, E-0381)

12:6FFE.name: DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex_Data4
12:6FFE.note: Twelve frame durations in frames (14 for frames 0-6, 54, 14, 14, 14, then 64) followed by four $FF bytes, for sprite set $1F. DrawFieldSprites_StepFrameLoop steps the frame in wObject5 + $7 through them and wraps to 0 at the $FF; the sub-index is not the frame number but the byte of DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex_Data5 for it. (C1, E-0381)

12:700E.name: DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex_Data5
12:700E.note: Twelve sub-index values, 0, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 0, 3, 4, 5, 6, followed by four $FF padding bytes, indexed by the frame number wObject5 + $7 (0-11) of sprite set $1F. DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex stores the byte in hSpriteSubIndex; the durations of the same frames are in DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex_Data4. (C1, E-0381)

12:701E.name: DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex_Data6
12:701E.note: A list of frame durations, 4, 7, 7, 4, ended by $FF: four frames for sprite set $1E. DrawFieldSprites_StepFrameLoop advances the frame in wObject5 + $7 when the counter wObject5 + $6 reaches the current duration and wraps to frame 0 at the $FF; the frame number is the sub-index. (C1, E-0381)

12:7023.name: DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex_Data7
12:7023.note: A list of frame durations, $20, $20, ended by $FF: two frames of 32 frames each, for sprite set $18. DrawFieldSprites_StepFrameLoop advances the frame in wObject5 + $7 when the counter wObject5 + $6 reaches the current duration and wraps to frame 0 at the $FF; the frame number is the sub-index. (C1, E-0381)

12:7026.name: DrawFieldSprites_AnimateSubIndex_Data8
12:7026.note: Eighteen (sub-index, duration) byte pairs and an $FF, $FF end mark, for sprite set $20: (0,30), (0,5), (1,4), (2,5), (1,4), (0,5), (1,4), (2,5), (3,4), (4,5), (3,4), (2,5), (5,4), (6,5), (5,4), (2,5), (1,4), (0,5). DrawFieldSprites_StepFramePairs steps pair wObject5 + $7 when the counter wObject5 + $6 reaches its duration and returns its sub-index for hSpriteSubIndex; at the end mark it stays on the last pair instead of wrapping. (C1, E-0381)

12:71BB.name: FindTriggerEntryForCurrentScreen_StoreTrigger_Data
12:71BB.note: 45 bytes, each a trigger kind 0-10 (0 means none), indexed by the second byte of the map object entry (wMapObjects) or screen trigger entry (wScreenTriggers) that was found for the screen. FindTriggerEntryForCurrentScreen_StoreTrigger uses it only when the low two bits of the entry first byte are 0 (otherwise those bits are the kind) and stores a non-zero result in wTriggerKind, which selects the marker graphics (TriggerSpriteTable) and sprite set (DrawTriggerMarkerSprite_Data1). (C1, E-0381)

12:7308.name: DrawTriggerMarkerSprite_Data1
12:7308.note: Eleven meta-sprite set numbers, indexed by wTriggerKind (0-10): $00, $09, $01, $01, $02, $03, $04, $05, $06, $07, $08. DrawTriggerMarkerSprite stores the byte in hSpriteSetIndex and draws that set (sub-index 0, tile offset $40) with DrawMetaSprite. (C1, E-0381)

12:7313.name: DrawTriggerMarkerSprite_Data2
12:7313.note: Sixteen (X, Y) pixel pairs, indexed by wTriggerCell times 2: ($10,$20), ($10,$70), ($20,$10), ($20,$40), ($20,$60), ($30,$30), ($40,$50), ($40,$70), ($50,$10), ($50,$30), ($60,$50), ($70,$20), ($70,$40), ($70,$70), ($80,$10), ($80,$60). DrawTriggerMarkerSprite uses them on special map types (wMapType bit 7) with no screen triggers, adding 8 to X and $10 to Y and the scroll for the marker origin; they are the cells of IsPlayerOnTriggerCell_Data multiplied by 16. (C1, E-0381)

12:752E.name: FieldState_WalkAMenu_CheckKeyWorldItemOnA_Data
12:752E.note: Eight packed screen coordinates, $01, $10, $12, $13, $20, $21, $23 and $32 (high nibble the screen X, low nibble the screen Y). FieldState_WalkAMenu_CheckKeyWorldItemOnA indexes it with a byte of the current floor entry in wKeyWorldFloorState, compares the result with the screen the player is on (hMapScreenX high, hMapScreenY low) and, when equal, starts talk event group $0E with the address of that floor entry in wScriptParam0 and wScriptParam1. (C1, E-0381)

12:7581.name: IsPlayerOnTriggerCell_Data
12:7581.note: Sixteen (X, Y) cell pairs, indexed by wTriggerCell times 2: (1,2), (1,7), (2,1), (2,4), (2,6), (3,3), (4,5), (4,7), (5,1), (5,3), (6,5), (7,2), (7,4), (7,7), (8,1), (8,6) (cells of 16 pixels). IsPlayerOnTriggerCell uses them on special map types other than $85; the player is on the trigger cell when its pixel X and Y divided by 16 equal the pair. DrawTriggerMarkerSprite_Data2 holds the same cells in pixels. (C1, E-0381)

14:4280.name: HibernateMenu_OptionCursor_DrawTile_Data
14:4280.note: Five little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank14): $0021, $0061, $00A1, $00E1 and $0121, which are rows 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 at column 1. HibernateMenu_OptionCursor_DrawTile indexes it with wGridCursorX times 2 and writes the tile B there, the cursor beside an option. (C1, E-0381)

14:4586.name: HibernateMenu_ChooseRecords_MarkAndRedraw_Data
14:4586.note: Five little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank14): $0021, $0061, $00A1, $00E1 and $0121, which are rows 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 at column 1; the same values as HibernateMenu_OptionCursor_DrawTile_Data. HibernateMenu_ChooseRecords_MarkAndRedraw indexes it with wListCursor times 2 and writes the mark tile $BC at the chosen entry. (C1, E-0381)

14:4F24.name: HibernateMenu_RestoreYesNoBox_Data1
14:4F24.note: Six tile ids, $B4 five times then $B5: a row of box border (five edge tiles and the right corner). HibernateMenu_RestoreYesNoBox copies it with HibernateMenu_CopyBoxRows (C = 4, one row) onto the first row of the yes/no box area at wWindowTileBuffer + $112, restoring the border of the box that lay under the yes/no box. (C1, E-0381)

14:4F2A.name: HibernateMenu_RestoreYesNoBox_Data2
14:4F2A.note: Six zero bytes: the CGB attribute bytes (palette 0, no flip) for the same six tiles as HibernateMenu_RestoreYesNoBox_Data1. On a CGB HibernateMenu_RestoreYesNoBox copies them with HibernateMenu_CopyBoxRows onto the first row of wWindowAttrBuffer + $112, with WRAM bank 2 mapped. (C1, E-0381)

14:605E.name: RunNameEntryStateWhenNotFading_KeyCursor_Data
14:605E.note: Five bytes, $10, $10, $10, $0D, $0D: the last key column of each key row of the name entry keyboard, indexed by wNameEntryCursorY (rows 0-4). The left and right moves of the keyboard cursor wrap at it: Left from column 0 goes to this column, and Right at this column goes back to column 0. (C1, E-0381)

14:688A.name: IsHLByteInList_Data
14:688A.note: A $FF-terminated list of 42 glyph codes: $3E-$42, $29-$35, $37, $38, $75-$79, $60-$6C, $6E, $6F, $26 and $5A. IsHLByteInList returns A = 0 when the byte at HL is in it; the name entry uses that to decide that a glyph may take the mark $8D after it. (C1, E-0381)

14:68CA.name: IsHLByteInList_2_Data
14:68CA.note: A $FF-terminated list of ten glyph codes: $3E-$42 and $75-$79, a subset of IsHLByteInList_Data. IsHLByteInList_2 returns A = 0 when the byte at HL is in it; the name entry uses that to decide that a glyph that already has the mark $8D may change it to $8E. (C1, E-0381)

14:697D.name: RunNameEntryStateWhenNotFading_DrawYesNoTile_Data
14:697D.note: Two little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank14_2): $012F and $016F, which are row 9 and row 11 at column 15. RunNameEntryStateWhenNotFading_DrawYesNoTile indexes it with wNameEntryMenuCursor times 2 and writes the tile B there, the cursor beside yes or no. (C1, E-0381)

14:6C56.name: CopyTileForNameEntryLength_Data1
14:6C56.note: Five little-endian VRAM addresses, $9500, $9510, $9520, $9530 and $9540: the tiles of the five name places. CopyTileForNameEntryLength indexes it with wNameEntryLength times 2 and copies the plain tile CopyTileForNameEntryLength_Data2 to that address. (C1, E-0381)

14:6C60.name: CopyTileForNameEntryLength_Data2
14:6C60.note: One 16-byte tile: $FF, $00 repeated eight times, which is a solid tile of colour 1 in the 2-bits-per-pixel format (low bit plane $FF, high plane $00). CopyTileForNameEntryLength copies it with CopyTileBytesToVRAM_Bank14 to the address picked from CopyTileForNameEntryLength_Data1. (C1, E-0381)

15:54E2.name: BreedMenu_ChooseParents_YesNoCursor_DrawTile_Data
15:54E2.note: Two little-endian word offsets into the BG map from the scroll position (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank15): $012D and $016D, which are row 9 and row 11 at column 13. BreedMenu_ChooseParents_YesNoCursor_DrawTile indexes it with wChoiceCursor times 2 and writes the tile B there, stepping back if the address wrapped. (C1, E-0381)

15:5A67.name: BreedMenu_ReturnToMap_CopySixteenTiles_Data1
15:5A67.note: Sixteen glyph ids ($A3, $50, $44, $11, $16, $19, $48, $24, $A6, $12, $31, $29, $32, $18, $14, $25). BreedMenu_ReturnToMap_CopySixteenTiles counts C from 16 down to 1 and reads the byte at offset C, so the byte at offset 0 is never read and for C = 16 it reads the byte after the table (the first byte of BreedMenu_ReturnToMap_CopySixteenTiles_Data2, $D0). The glyph tile is taken from GlyphFont in bank $1F (16 bytes each) and copied to word C of BreedMenu_ReturnToMap_CopySixteenTiles_Data2. (C1, E-0381)

15:5A77.name: BreedMenu_ReturnToMap_CopySixteenTiles_Data2
15:5A77.note: Sixteen words (32 bytes), each a VRAM tile address: $8ED0, $8EE0, $8EF0, $8F50, $8F60, $8F70, $8FD0, $8FE0, $8FF0, then $9700 to $9760 in steps of $10. BreedMenu_ReturnToMap_CopySixteenTiles counts C from 16 down to 1 and uses word C as the destination of the 16-byte tile it copies from GlyphFont for glyph BreedMenu_ReturnToMap_CopySixteenTiles_Data1[C], so word 0 is never used and the pass with C = 16 reads the two bytes after the table. (C1, E-0381)

15:6566.name: DrawThreeOptionCursorTile_Data
15:6566.note: Three words that are offsets from the BG map entry at the top left of the visible screen (BGMapAddressAtScroll_Bank15): $0021, $0061, $00A1, which are rows 1, 3 and 5 of column 1. DrawThreeOptionCursorTile indexes them with wGridCursorX and writes tile B (the cursor or blank tile its caller chose) at that entry. (C1, E-0381)

15:6937.name: TestBitInFieldAtArg3_Data
15:6937.note: Eight single-bit masks $80, $40, $20, $10, $08, $04, $02, $01. TestBitInFieldAtArg3 takes the bit number in wArg1:wArg2, finds the byte at wArg3:wArg4 plus bit number / 8, ANDs it with entry (bit number AND 7) and sets wArg5 to $FF when the bit is set, else 0; bit 0 of the field is therefore the top bit of its first byte. (C1, E-0381)

15:6DD0.name: ShowSaveFileInfoWindow_Data1
15:6DD0.note: Three words, addresses of cells in wWindowTileBuffer (rows of 20 bytes): $C3A8, $C3D0, $C3F8, which are rows 8, 10 and 12 of column 8. ShowSaveFileInfoWindow indexes them with the entry number (0 up to the count byte read at sSavedPlayerName + $F1) and stores tile $EA in the cell and tile $ED in the cell after it. (C1, E-0381)

15:6E08.name: ShowSaveFileInfoWindow_Data2
15:6E08.note: Three words, addresses in wWindowTileBuffer: $C3AA, $C3D2, $C3FA, which are rows 8, 10 and 12 of column 10. For each saved entry ShowSaveFileInfoWindow takes the number in byte $62 of its record (masked with $7F), makes digit tiles ($E0 + digit) with HLToDecimalDigits and writes the tens digit (only when it is not 0) at the word picked by the entry number and the ones digit in the next cell.
